data.title: Inappropriate activation of the TSC/Rheb/mTOR/S6K cassette induces IRS1/2 depletion, insulin resistance, and cell survival deficiencies
data.authors: Shah OJ; Wang Zhiyong; Hunter T

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: The companion paper to Harrington 2004, published two months later. In cultured mammalian cells, constitutive Rheb/mTOR/S6K activity depletes IRS1 and IRS2, producing cellular insulin resistance and impaired survival signalling. Together the two papers establish the S6K1 -> IRS negative feedback arm.
data.abstract_excerpt: Tuberous sclerosis is a largely benign tumor syndrome derived from the acquisition of somatic lesions in genes encoding the tumor suppressor products, TSC1 or TSC2. Loss of function of the TSC1-TSC2 complex, which acts as a Rheb GAP, yields constitutive, unrestrained signaling from the cell growth machinery comprised of Rheb, mTOR, and S6K. We demonstrate herein that constitutive activation of the Rheb/mTOR/S6K cassette, whether by genetic deletion of TSC1 or TSC2 or by ectopic expression of Rheb, is sufficient to induce insulin resistance.

extracted_findings.effect: Constitutive mTOR/S6K signalling depletes IRS1/2 and causes cellular insulin resistance
